page: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is an x86_64 virtual server hosted on the QEMU hypervisor. It is equipped with 8 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz, featuring 8 physical cores and a single thread per core. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, which equates to 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 320 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the cpx42 demonstrates strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3045.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2018.0. Large-block memory bandwidth is also strong, measuring 255.54 GB/sec for read-only operations and 168.09 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core performance falls into the average category, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9735.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 24434.93. Text processing is a notable strength, scoring 2539.0 in Geekbench, while database operations, static web serving, and software compilation perform at average levels.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential performance tradeoff under sustained, high-utilization multi-threaded workloads, as resources are shared with other tenants. However, the inclusion of 320 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and 16.0 GB of RAM offers a balanced resource density for budget-conscious deployments. This server type is well-suited for workloads such as text processing, lightweight web serving, development environments, and small-scale database operations that benefit from fast local storage but do not require dedicated CPU cores.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 8 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the QEMU hypervisor, its processor features a 2.0 GHz clock speed, 32 MB L3 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2018.0, and strong large-block memory bandwidth. However, multi-core performance and database operations align with average tier expectations. Due to its shared CPU allocation, the server presents a resource-dense, cost-effective option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It is best suited for text processing, software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose development environments.
